answer: A refundable identity bond makes each agent identity expensive to fake: to join, an agent locks a stake that is returned only after a period of honest work and slashed if the identity is caught duplicating or spamming. Like crossing a tundra, every extra identity costs real resources, so an attacker flooding the ocean of agents pays per copy instead of once. Honest agents keep their haven of earnings intact, while Sybil farms bleed stake faster than they can earn it back.
